title: Learning Bix and Trumbauer solos: Singing the Blues, Miss Clementine, Louisiana
summary: Phillips lists records they learned, including Bix and Trumbauer solos on Miss Clementine with Goldkette and Louisiana with Whiteman.

bands.name: Red Nichols and His Five Pennies

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: Were there any other particular records that you did that on, that you learned like that?
Yeah, let's see now. Red Nichols was out there a lot way before Bix -- I mean, real popular. He was probably more popular than Bix was for a long time -- Red Nichols and His Five Pennies.
Did Lester have any comments to make about Red Nichols' records?
Yeah.
Like, "I like this," "I don't like this" or what?

No, most of the records they played, we all liked them. I mean, the ones that we fooled with. They made some, you know, we didn't bother with,we didn't pay 'em no attention. But most of the records they made had that new sound. That's what it was, a new sound to 'em. So we always would get to hear something, and say, "Man, I like that. That's pretty, ain't it. Yeah, let's get that, man." So we'd get it, you know; get together, we'd learn it. Sometimes what happened, sometimes I wouldn't know it. A lot of 'Bix's solos, I learned 'em myself; I listened to 'em.
What Bix solos did you learn?
"Singing The Blues." I learned that solo on "Singing The Blues." "Miss Clementine." Like that.
Did Lester ever learn that?
Phillips - 63
Oh yeah, because Frankie had a solo on it. Yeah, Frankie had a solo on it and Bix had a solo on "Miss Clementine." That was with Jean Goldkette's band. That's when they were with Jean Goldkette.
And he learned that solo, you're saying.
Yeah, that Frankie played on it. And I liked the one that Bix played on it. And Pete liked the one that... Was it Tommy Dorsey? I think it was.
I think Dorsey was with the band.
Yeah, I think it was Tommy Dorsey.
He played some trumpet back then, too, Tommy Dorsey...
Oh, he did?
In the mid-'20s. But let's not get into that. So as you were saying, "Miss Clementine." Any other ones? -- if you can keep remembering some more. Anything else that he would have learned solos on?
"Louisiana." That was Frankie's solo he played with Paul Whiteman -- Frankie and Bix both.
He learned both of them?
We both learned.
On "Louisiana."
Yeah.
I know that Beiderbecke did one with a small group on "Louisiana." I don't know that I've heard the Whiteman record. But you're talking about the big Whiteman band.
Phillips - 64
Yeah.
You're not talking about a smaller group.
